links.reason: Both are paalai poems on leaving for wealth, but 43 calls leaving a companion for ஏதில் பொருட்பிணி a மடமை and 53 says the man's நெஞ்சம் cannot hide when 'இல்லோர்க்கு இல்' is said; these are different situations, not incompatible claims. 43 has no woman speaking, so 'the woman left behind refuses to call either grace' is true only of 53.

The patikam line 'விஞ்சைக்கு இறைவன் மகள் வீணையில் தோற்ற வாறும்' announces the outcome and 659 shows the suitors' playing mocked by the birds (அசிப்ப போன்று); the later verse prepares the announced victory rather than contradicting it. No incompatible claim, so 'tension' is the wrong type; the note also says the kings 'fail before her' where the verse only has birds fleeing.

1915 has Vijayai say 'யானலன் ஔவை யாவாள் சுநந்தையே', a claim of motherhood; 2646 has a grieving cry 'சுநந்தை நீ ஔவை அல்லை' addressed to the departing woman, rhetoric not a counter-claim. The speaker of 2646 is uncertain (Nandattan or Civakan), and the teaches line about the mother 'made true by love' depends on it being Civakan.

Verse 2 recalls the 'அரியேறு போழ்ந்த செங்கண் நெடியான்' and 409 has the seer say 'திங்கள் நாள் அகவையில் திவிட்டன் ... சிங்கம் வாய் பிளந்திடும்', so the poet's announced feat is tied to a date within the story. Prediction and later report of the same deed fit 'develops'.

1803 'முன்னுரைத்த மூன்று கனவும் புணையாக' does point back to the king's reading in 225, so the dream-and-recollection link is real. But 1803 says nothing of the unexplained falling tree, so 'the part she could not afford to hear' is the note's inference, not what the verse states.

34 'தொல்வினை துரப்ப ஓடி விலங்கிடைச் சுழன்ற போது' recalls animal births; Siddhar 130 'போதும் என்பது எக்காலம்' is a plea over births as stone, tree, fish, bird. Nothing in 34 is a cry of 'enough' that the pair 'will act on', and the epic does not gain a first-person plea from the Siddhar; the shared ground is births driven by deeds, a theme.

1552 'செருக்கிய களியன் ஆனான்' says nothing of the source of his fortune, and the teaches line concedes 'the verse says no such thing'. Naladiyar 93 (செல்வம் ... விடுக்கும் வினை உலந்தக் கால்) is brought in as a karmic gloss the epic does not offer, which is a shared theme, not a qualification.

1165 'சினமெனப் பட்ட தீயுட் பிறந்தது செருக்கு' is a warrior's boast; Tirumanthiram 266 'மலிந்தவர் மாளும் துணையும் ஒன்றின்றி மெலிந்த சினத்தினுள் வீழ்ந்தொழிந்தாரே' gives no origin of pride from anger and the 'மலிந்தவர்' are not clearly the proud. The 'no face or voice' gain has no basis in 266. Only the word சினம் is shared.

Vijayai's 'யாரையுந் தேறன்மின்' (with the order to tell none but Nambi) is a blanket distrust against the couplet's 'தேறற்க யாரையும் தேராது தேர்ந்தபின் தேறுக'; the contrast of examined and unexamined trust is real. But 509 concerns choosing men for tasks, while 1815 is secrecy about an heir, so the pairing is a limiting case that needs a generous reading. No four-word run is shared.

2573 never names the friend (the line 'பேரிடர் தன்க ணீக்கிப் யாய தோழற்' is corrupt) and 945 has the dog whisper of the five mantras; the link depends on identifying the friend as the yaksha, which the Tamil does not say. The 'first public memorial the epic records' is also unsupported by the verse.

106 gives the reason as 'நிற்கும் செவ்வினை நீங்க நின்றனர்', the wearing away of karma, while Naladiyar 21 says even elephant-borne kings 'துஞ்சினார் என்றெடுத்துத் தூற்றப்பட்டார்'. Abdication as an 'answer to death' is the note's reading; the epic's own stated reason is different.

The Kural's 'கேள்போல் பகைவர் தொடர்பு' (fear the friendly-seeming foe) is shown by the usurper who 'நிகழ்வது ஓரான் மகிழ்வெய்தி' and praises the returned beasts as double his own. The scene adds the victim's blindness and that the kin-like foe is on the favoured side. The verse is flagged uncertain but the point rests on 'ஓரான்'.

899 'தோற்று வந்து என் சிலம்படி கைதொழ' sets the vow, and 2088 'சிலம்பின்மேற் சென்னி சேர்த்தி ... ஊடல் நீக்கினான்' has him bow on her anklets; the later verse fulfils the vow. The quarrel plea 'சிறியவர் செய்த தீமை பெரியவர் பொறுப்பர்' shows it as a lover's tactic, not a defeat admitted.

Both rebuke those who see kings fall and stay unmoved (71 'கண்டால் மயங்காதே', 286 'கண்டு பின்னும்'). But 71 never says effort suffices without a god; 'ஊக்கஞ் செய்தியேல் சித்தி படர்தல்' is silence about grace, and the note itself grants the tension holds only on a reading the verse does not state.

702 'நோற்றனள் அங்கை' is the women's idiom that she must have done penance for such a husband; Kural 265 'வேண்டிய வேண்டியாங் கெய்தலால் செய்தவம்' gives wanting-and-getting as the motive of tapas. The link needs the claim that the idiom rests on the Kural's doctrine, which the verse does not show; no four-word run is shared.

1992 grades giving as தலை, இடை, கடை by receiver, giver and gift; Tirumanthiram 505 says a gift to those without சீலம் and நோன்பு is a 'காலங் கழிந்த பயிர்'. Both turn on the worth of the receiver, but the teaches line ('the lowest grade may still be a gift') is not in 1992 and is vague.

61 'கிணை நிலைப் பொருநர் தம் செல்லல் கீழ்ப் படப்' shares the kinai bard's want with the Sirupanarruppadai passage of the kinai-woman's unsalted greens (உப்பிலி வெந்ததை). That is a shared figure, and nothing in 61 shows it draws on that passage. The other side gains only a generic contrast.

2149 'கள்ளத்தால் உயிரை உண்ணக் கருதினோம்' answers Kattiyangaran's guile against Govindan's party, while 259 has him say the king may go to heaven and he will guard the earth, with no word of guile. The 'symmetry named outright' is Govindan's reply to a plot on himself, not to the throne-winning in 259.

Pazhamozhi 109 'புலிமுகத்து உண்ணி பறித்து விடல்' (good done to the graceless brings danger) and Sirupanchamoolam 16 'நாய்வாயுள் நல்ல தசை' (good meat in a dog's mouth) state wasted versus dangerous kindness to the base. Together they separate two costs; the line 3 of 16 is hard but the closing image is clear.

3081 'எரி முழக்கம் அன்ன சுக்கிலத் தியானம் என்னும் கணை' uses fire only as a simile for an arrow of meditation; Tirumanthiram 219 'அங்கி வினை சுடுமாமே' is a claim about a worshipped fire. The shared word is fire, and 'disagree on where the fire is' makes a simile into a doctrine.

14 pairs the dog and the elephant on one day ('அன்றைப் பகலே ... களிற்றை வென்ற வாறும்'), and 985 has Civakan beating the elephant 'இளையாட்கு உடைந்து' and going to the garden. The teaches line, that both deeds were mercy and not courtship with love coming after, rests on verses 974-984 that are not in the packet; 985 itself does not say it.

73 has 'மருளுரை பயிற்றி மன்னிய வேடம் ... வீதி நடுவினில் வந்தான்'; Kural 585 'கடாஅ உருவொடு கண்ணஞ்சாது'. A madman's guise is a classic unsuspected form, so calling it a conspicuous exception to 585 is the note's reading, and the verse does not say every eye is drawn to him.

1040 has the maiden pray 'பிறவிநோய் பெயர்க'; 1107 has onlookers, not her, go to the forest ('மாதவம் போகுவாரும்') or turn back amazed ('கனவினும் என்ன'). Different persons and no incompatible claim, so 'the wedding closes on the same two answers' is a loose parallel.

Both use a lamp whose fuel is spent: 2316 'நெய்யும் திரியும் சென்றற்ற போழ்தே ... இருவினை சென்று தேய்ந்தால்' and Naladiyar 51 'விளக்குநெய் தேய்விடத்து ... நல்வினை தீர்விடத்து நிற்குமாம் தீது'. The shared lamp-and-deeds image is real, but one does not extend the other, so same_image fits; counting both deeds as fuel is a good point.

647 'பகை அல்லாதவரைப் பகை ஆக்கலும் ... வெதுப்புமே' partly matches Kural 871 'பகை என்னும் பண்பிலதனை ... வேண்டற்பாற்று அன்று', and adds a second warning about the ill-hearted. The teaches line cites 'Kural 879' and 'rival counsel' of 643-644, neither in the packet, so it misdescribes the pair.

908 'பொருந்திற் பொருந்துக ... அழிப்பார் ஒன்று சிந்தையள்' and 1050 'இறத்தல் ஒன்றோ ... செய்தவம் முயறல் ஒன்றோ' show two women bound to Civakan by vows. They are parallel resolves by two speakers, not one unit developing the other, and the contest outcome is not in either verse.

109 has the court affirm 'ஒரு குடை நீழல் காக்கும்' of Tivittan; 722 only shows the lion's power and the gods trembling (பனித்தார்). The verse does not show Tivittan tested by it, so 'the hall's affirmation is tested' is the note's plot, not what 722 says.

2293 'மிறைக் கொளீஇ திருத்துவான்' and Purananuru 284 'மிறையாகத் திரிந்த வாய்வாள் திருத்தா' share the bent sword straightened on a lever, with the enemy then fleeing (அஞ்சி ... இரிந்திட்டாரே; பெயர்புறம் நகுமே). The shared wording is distinctive, and the changes (laugh to fear) are real; the claim that he dies in the next verse is not checkable here.

2922 only calls the women to 'உறுதி கேண்மின்', and states no teaching; 2906 'மேல் விளையாத இன்பம் இல்லை' ranks kingly joy highest. Placing the two as limit and rule rests on later verses, so this is sequence, not qualification.

1556 'மகளிர்தம் வலையிற் பட்டான்' and 1624 'புருவ வில்லால் ... பகழியால் அழுத்தப் பட்டான்' present the same event in two images, the net then bow and arrows. It is the same fall told twice, and the 'quarrel's cause returns' is not in 1624.

42 says even the lords of the gods who had Indra's splendour 'தந்திரு உருவம் பொன்றித் தளர்ந்தனர் அனந்தம்', while Naladiyar 21 says even elephant-borne kings 'எஞ்சினார் இவ்வுலகத்தில்' none. The epic carries the visible impermanence of kings up to the gods, which is a real extension, and the Naladiyar gives the human instance the doctrine rests on.

1136 'அஞ்சினன் மறைத்துச் சின்னாள்' shows the minister hiding bad news and sending a go-between, but nowhere says the king cannot bear bitter words; Kural 389 'செவி கைப்பச் சொற்பொறுக்கும் பண்புடை வேந்தன்' is brought in by the note's own gloss of the king as proud, which is not in the verse.

1188 'நிலையின் நிழல் தானது நின்று கொடுத்து' and Kalittokai 11 'தன் நிழலைக் கொடுத்து அளிக்கும் கலை' share the stag shading the doe, a distinctive palai figure. But the other two creatures are in 1187, not here, and 'a lone traveller with no beloved at home' is not in the verse (the hearer is Civakan, who is married).

1435 has Arukkan claim 'இது மறிதல் இல்லை மறிப்பவர் பிறரும் இல்லை' and 1439 has the hostile 'சலம்புரி தெய்வம் அஞ்சித் தன்னுரு அடைந்தது'. A claim and the scene that answers it is a sound shape, but the refutation rests on reading 'சலம்புரி தெய்வம்' as the missile's deity from verses not in the packet, and both verses are flagged uncertain.

57 'நாகம் மிக் கதங்கொண்டு' is a plain tale of a prince subduing a raging elephant; nothing in it makes the elephant a figure for the senses, and the word மதம் is not in it. Tirumanthiram 2023 'ஆக மதத்தன ஐந்து களிறு' is an allegory; joining them reads the allegory into the story.

21 has the king (யான் இவ் வாளினின் மக்கள் இரட்டை ... பலி) hold that killing is the right worship, and Kural 259 'ஒன்றன் உயிர்செகுத்து உண்ணாமை நன்று' ranks abstaining above a thousand sacrifices. The note correctly gives the claim to the king, not the work, and the conflict holds on the reading that 259 bears on blood offerings.

2235 'பிணமாலைப் பேய்மகட்குப் பெருவிருந்து' and Purananuru 26 'முடித் தலை அடுப்பாக ... அடுகளம் வேட்ட' both show the battlefield as a feast, the dead cooked or served. Qualifies does not fit, since the epic does not limit the Sangam poem; it is a shared image told from the slain's side.

698 'நின்ற ஒளியோடு ஒழுகப் படும்' (honour the light he stands in) and 388 'இறையென்று வைக்கப் படும்' (a king is counted a god if he rules justly) do touch on the king's standing. But the teaches line only says that 'other readings remove the conflict', which is no lesson, and the note rests on a commentator's reading.

1357 'மான மாமணி வீழ்த்து' shames flight as lost honour and 1380 'ஒருவனை ஒருவன் அஞ்சி ஓடுமேல் அருவருப்புடைய ஆண்மை' calls it loathsome. They are two taunts on the same theme from different speakers; neither develops the other, and 'one argument in two voices' is just the shared theme.

The note says both verses ask goddess, rare bird or human; 1017 asks 'வானவர் மகள்கொல் விஞ்சை மாதுகொள் மண்ணுளாள்கொல்', goddess's daughter, Vidyadhara woman or earthly woman, with no bird. Kural 1081 'அணங்குகொல் ஆய்மயில்கொல்' has the peahen; the options differ, so 'the same three-way wonder' misdescribes the verse.

1585 'காப்பியக் கவிகள் காம வெரியெழ விகற்பித்திட்டார்' has Civakan call beauty a skin-bag painted with brows and eyes, while 1482 'புருவத் தாற் புடைத்து ... இளமுலை கொல்லுமே' has him speak of the same features as weapons killing him. The later verse sets the hero against his own earlier rapture and names the genre the poem belongs to; the 'wife versus another's' part is surplus.

1798 'வெம்முலைகளோடு அவர்கள் காதல் மிக வீங்க' shows desire swelling as she enters, and Naladiyar 17 'வேல்கண்ணள் என்றிவளை வெஃகன்மின் ... கோல்கண்ணளாகும்' warns that the spear-eyed will stoop with a staff. The age limit is supplied by the quatrain and not the verse; it is a general theme set beside a scene, not a test of the quatrain.

1177 'தம்வினை கழுவுகின்றார் சாரணர்' has ascetics wash their own karma, a plain phrase, and Tirumanthiram 2422 'அறுவை அழுக்கேற்றி ஏற்றல்போல் ஆகுவதெல்லாம் அருட்பாசமாகுமே' calls what comes to the soul the bond of grace. Self-effort against grace is a possible conflict, but the 'washer is grace' reading is not in the verse (flagged uncertain) and the epic's phrase is not an image of cloth-washing.

even a dog without merit may be reborn a god, as iron in the forge becomes gold

passing beyond kingship and its pleasures is the right course

pleasures enjoyed through many days in heaven prove vain when death nears
wealth, foes and wives and children can be had, but a brother cannot be made
the unwise spend the store of good deeds on pleasure and perish
